paperTitle: LABORAL: A Transformational Game for LER/DORT Prevention through Gesture-Interactions
centralContribution: This work introduces LABORAL, a transformational game designed for hand stretching using gesture-interactions, aiming to prevent and educate users about occupational diseases such as LER (Lesão por Esforço Repetitivo) / RSI (Repetitive Strain Injury) and DORT (Distúrbio Osteomuscular Relacionado ao Trabalho) / WMSD (Work-Related Musculoskeletal Disorder), particularly for individuals who perform repetitive computer movements. The game fosters engaging learning and behavioral transformation regarding upper limb health.

elements.name: Paper Abstract
elements.description: The increasing informatization of workplaces leads to prolonged occupational computer use, causing pain and severe occupational diseases like LER/DORT, which primarily affect upper limbs. While occupational gymnastics are preventive, their implementation is often lacking. Gesture recognition technologies, like the Leap Motion sensor, offer engaging alternatives for motor rehabilitation. This paper introduces LABORAL, a 3D transformational game developed with Unity and Leap Motion, focusing on precise, physiotherapist-defined stretching exercises to prevent LER/DORT, extending previous research by targeting specific therapeutic movements.
elements.justification: This element provides a concise overview of the paper's context, problem, methodology, and aim, which is fundamental for understanding the entire work.

elements.name: Central Contribution of LABORAL Game
elements.description: LABORAL is introduced as a transformational game for hand stretching, utilizing gesture-interactions to prevent and educate users about occupational diseases like LER/DORT. Its primary innovation lies in fostering engaging learning and behavioral transformation concerning upper limb health, particularly for individuals performing repetitive computer movements, by precisely implementing physiotherapist-defined stretching exercises.
elements.justification: This element directly states the core innovation and purpose of the paper, making it the most critical conceptual extract.

elements.name: LABORAL Game System Architecture
elements.description: A conceptual representation of the LABORAL game's architecture, illustrating its development with the Unity engine, the integration of the Leap Motion sensor for real-time gestural interaction, and the user interface design featuring pose cards, recognition indicators, exercise names, and a countdown timer. It demonstrates how these components collaborate to facilitate interactive hand stretching exercises.
elements.justification: This element provides a high-level visual understanding of how the game's core components (Unity, Leap Motion, UI) are integrated to deliver the central contribution.

elements.name: User Interface for Hand Pose Imitation
elements.description: A visual depiction of the LABORAL game's user interface, highlighting the sequence of 'cards' displaying reference hand poses for the user to imitate. It also shows the black-outlined square for real-time pose recognition, the exercise name on the left, and a 10-second countdown timer on the top-left, which guides the player and provides immediate feedback.
elements.justification: Understanding the user interface is critical to grasping how players interact with the game and how the therapeutic exercises are presented and recognized.

elements.name: Defined Physiotherapy Stretching Sequences
elements.description: A table outlining the five fundamental hand stretching sequences defined by a collaborating physiotherapist, designed to target specific occupational conditions like tendinitis, carpal tunnel syndrome, and epicondylitis. Each sequence's name, the number of poses it includes, and examples of target conditions are provided.
elements.justification: This table directly presents the therapeutic content and structure of the game's exercises, which are central to its preventative goal for LER/DORT.

elements.name: Median Pose Recognition Times for Individual Exercises
elements.description: A graph illustrating the median recognition times for the 17 individual physiotherapy poses when detected by the Leap Motion sensor. It highlights the variability in recognition speed across different poses, with open hands generally being easier and certain complex or closed-hand poses taking significantly longer to recognize.
elements.justification: This element quantifies the performance of the core technology (Leap Motion) in recognizing the individual therapeutic gestures, which is vital for the game's efficacy.

elements.name: Sequential Exercise Test Results: Execution Time and Failures
elements.description: A comprehensive table presenting the average continuous execution times, the types of poses that frequently caused failures, and the overhead time compared to discrete pose recognition for each of the five defined exercise sequences. This data highlights the practical challenges in continuous gesture recognition.
elements.justification: This table summarizes the main experimental results, demonstrating the practical performance of the game's sequences and highlighting specific recognition challenges in a continuous gameplay context.

elements.name: Leap Motion Recognition Limitations and Challenges
elements.description: A conceptual illustration or detailed description of the Leap Motion sensor's difficulties in consistently recognizing specific hand movements. This includes challenges with closed hands (e.g., Supination, Pronation) and claw positions, as well as occasional temporary disconnections potentially due to overheating, indicating areas for future system improvement.
elements.justification: This element addresses the practical limitations and unresolved issues of the underlying technology, crucial for a complete understanding of the system's current state and future research directions.
